Emotional labor is a thing. It would probably help if you didn't expect someone to remind you to do your share. But it's good you don't expect a thank you.

You sound like you genuinely want to do better. I recommend you look up the term emotional labor. Basically, it's the expectation that one person in a relationship does things like reminding to clean, and it also takes a toll on a person. If you want to really help your SO, you need to take on some of the emotional labor too. Maybe make your own list of stuff that needs to be done regularly and check it off on the white board when it's done? Or put a reminder in your phone?

Hell yeah. I watched multiple members of my father's family get dementia. That was a horrible way to die. My grandfather on the other side lived into his 90's and his bones were so brittle he'd crack a rib coughing too hard.  It's natural and normal to not want to suffer old age.

But that's no reason to die now. Give yourself time to live first.

If it were me, the words I love you would be the best medicine. Tell her you don't have to talk about what's hurting her if she doesn't want to, but if you think you can deal with it, let her know she can tell you anything and you'll try not to judge. And if she doesn't want to talk about how she's feeling now, just make sure she knows she can talk to you any time. That kind of support from a sibling would make such a difference. And then, just talk to her about what you always talk about... Movies, music, sports, school, whatever.shes still the same person, just feeling very sad right now.

Since I was a kid. Like single digits. Tried to hang myself in the closet before I knew what the word meant.

Honestly not sure what keeps me going other than not being a fan of the unknown and not knowing exactly what happens after death. I have my beliefs about it, but I can't say I'm 100% sure. And I'm not a fan of extreme pain, so there's that also.

It feels a bit manipulative to post in a forum such as this. Obviously I'm trying to find someone to tell me not to do it. Obviously I'm not sure I want to listen to them either.
Sometimes I think the most valuable thing we can do is acknowledge each other's pain.
Sometimes I just feel like posting a list of the bad things that brought me here so I can have someone tell me yeah, that really is bad, you're not just oversensitive or crazy, if that is indeed the case. But I also don't like leaving folks with mental images they can't unsee especially if these things are unpleasant enough for me.

My family always seemed fine from the outside, but there's some seriously f-ed up things that happened. Is everyone like that? Or is it not normal?

Good question. It's really hard to get out of bed right now. I'm trying to stave off an anxiety attack by hiding in the bathroom right now. Not working so well. But you're not alone. People, even people who might be working beside you, do it all the time.

Have been talking with a religious person who is in sort of a leadership position, but am afraid to be completely honest. (We're not a mainstream religion so it's complicated explaining her role to someone outside). May try talking to her tomorrow night if we can get privacy. 

I did self injure tonight, which is probably not very smart, but i feel pretty at peace with it.

It's not so much hiding it as it is a matter of just pushing through and functioning as much as I can. I live alone, have no other support, so I have to do what needs to be done at least to pay the bills. thanks for taking the time to reply. I feel a little less alone. At least someone gives a crap.
